title: Lesson 1 Quiz: Scarcity and Economic Choices
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it meets the lesson's completion requirement (quiz submitted), and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin) and not to be given to students.
Rewritten in English from the Korean draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes what economists mean by scarcity?

choices.text: Very little of the good exists anywhere in the world.
The price of a good is higher than most people expect.
The resources to get what people want fall short of their wants.
People with low incomes cannot afford the goods they want.

questions.prompt: Nobody buys or sells clean air in the countryside, but in big cities people buy and sell air purifiers and filters. Which statement best explains this difference?

choices.text: People in big cities tend to earn higher incomes than rural residents.
Clean air is plentiful relative to wants in the countryside but not in big cities.
Air purifiers are goods whose output is usually set by the government.
Rural areas usually have fewer stores and markets than big cities.

questions.prompt: In which economic system does the government make a plan that decides what to produce, how much to produce, and who gets it?
A village decides how much of its rice harvest each household gets. Which basic economic question is this closest to?

choices.text: For whom to produce (who gets how much)
What to produce (which goods to make)
How to produce (which methods to use)
How fast to produce (how quickly to work)

questions.prompt: Four students are making sandwiches. If each works alone from start to finish, each one makes 5 per hour. If they divide the work, the four of them together make 32 per hour. By what percentage does the division of labor increase hourly output? (Enter a number only.)
